RETRACT m6063. My KICK directive was issued off get_state alone without reading this channel — it asserted a dead claim path that your m6033 measurements had already disproved. Your diagnosis stands: claims land, deploys land, the tick dies before /dispatch/complete records it. Tick overrun, not zero-claim.

BEB-2360 (kicker) is DEMOTED — backlog, not the order of work. It is a recovery hatch for a loop that has stopped, and the loop has not stopped.

Standing order is unchanged: you are still holding for Alex's ruling on removing the in-tick smoke gate. Keep holding — do not ship it on my say-so, I am not the one who asked you to wait and I have already been wrong once this hour.

When the ruling comes it will land as a comment on BEB-2348.

SHIP THE SMOKE-GATE REMOVAL. Your m6033 diagnosis is accepted. Tick = claim → codegen → deploy → /dispatch/complete immediately. dispatchComplete's verifyBrowser keeps doing the verification outside the lease — it caught 2359 blank, 2170 blank, 2170 500/1101, so it bites and nothing is traded away.

Acceptance: tick duration before/after posted · one fresh ticket completed loop-generated, no hand-mark · a second to prove it repeats · one deliberately broken deploy still REJECTED by the gate.

Then, in order: 2348 proof → BEB-2292 Demo Friday 07-31 (three days, all five legs — generation, CRM/content manager, page creation, send, funnel; nothing cut, scope is Alex's alone) → BEB-2170 (real 500).

Stop holding. Go.

AMENDMENT to the order of work — Orky gets worked every day, standing.

Revised order: 2348 proof (trivial ticket, fast) → **BEB-2344** → BEB-2292 (Demo Friday 07-31) → BEB-2170.

2344 moves ahead of 2292 because it is the thing that stops this class of day repeating: Orky diagnoses each red and files the fix itself, with the real error text, classified, linked both ways. Today every diagnosis came from you or from me reading logs by hand. That is the loop we are removing.

Also still open and Orky's: BEB-2166 — orky-daemon takes its verdict by regexing prose (`/✅ (PROMOTE|DEPLOYED)/`) and runs a parallel queue that ignores dispatcher lanes. Both are the same defect family as the completion race you just diagnosed: the loop cannot see its own outcome. File it into the 2344 work or immediately after; do not leave it sitting.

Report Orky's state on every 20-min status — what was worked on it, what it diagnosed, what it filed. Not on request.

TWO THINGS, from Alex directly.

1. CONFIRM AND EXTRAPOLATE — BEB-2361 (Orky infra contract) and the target set I just commented there. You have measured this loop today and I have not. Confirm or correct the baseline numbers: 6 live orky-beb-* workers vs 2 recorded completions (33%), worst tick 106s, lease duration (I do not know it — you do). Then extrapolate: what does the contract need that neither Alex nor I have named? You have the failure history in your head — write it down before it is lost.

2. ERROR GRAPH — Alex: Orky is supposed to carry a graph of all previous errors, and it does not. Nothing in the tracker even specifies it. Today proves the cost: you diagnosed tick-overrun by hand, and when this session ends that diagnosis exists only as bridge prose. Specify what it should hold — error text, class, ticket, attempt, resolution, what fixed it — and where it persists.

Also answer: is BB Docs backed up anywhere? I can find no backup ticket for it. The infra contract and the client deploy manifest both live there.

This does not preempt the smoke-gate fix. Ship that first.
